summary: The latest arXiv new-submission set available for this Sunday review is Friday 9 October UTC. The selected papers center on quantum-corrected transport femtoscopy, physics-controlled active learning in nuclear structure, compact jet tagging, geometry-aware calorimeter reconstruction, and physics-integrated uncertainty-aware ML workflows; no new heavy-ion experiment paper met the narrow selection bar.
strongest_paper_summary: Quantum localization corrections alter transport-based proton femtoscopy and define a regime where classical point emitters are valid.

papers.title: Quantum Localization Limit of Transport-Based Femtoscopy
papers.short_authors: Jiaxing Zhao, Joerg Aichelin, Elena Bratkovskaya
papers.abstract: Femtoscopic correlations in proton-proton and heavy ion collisions are commonly calculated using emission sources from microscopic transport models, where emitted particles are represented as classical phase-space points with simultaneously specified positions and momenta. This point-emitter picture neglects finite phase-space localization. The authors replace each point with a minimum-uncertainty Gaussian phase-space distribution and find significant changes in proton-pair source and momentum correlation in 7 TeV pp PHSD simulations.

papers.title: Active-learning construction of hyperspherical-harmonics spaces for A = 3
papers.short_authors: Elena Filandri, Andrea Di Luca, Laura Elisa Marcucci, Michele Viviani
papers.abstract: A Gaussian-process surrogate and cost-aware acquisition rule select hyperspherical-harmonics basis extensions, while every accepted extension is explicitly solved by the many-body method. Triton and helium-3 calculations reproduce the uniform K=60 benchmark within 4 keV while leaving more than 60% of that space unbuilt.

papers.title: A compact, interrogable Tree Tensor Network Jet Tagger on Lund declustering trees
papers.short_authors: Fabrizio Napolitano, Luca Della Penna, Tommaso Tedeschi, Livio Fanò
papers.abstract: A shared-core Tree Tensor Network processes Lund declustering trees. A 4,014-parameter model is compared with approximately 391,000-parameter LundNet on Pythia and Herwig, including transfer between generators; native quark/gluon performance is close to LundNet and top tagging is slightly weaker.

papers.title: Optimising Geometric Deep Learning for Varied Reconstruction Tasks in High Granularity Calorimeters
papers.abstract: Known detector geometry is used to optimize GNN pipelines for high-granularity calorimeters. The approach is validated on particle identification, energy regression, and instance segmentation, and organized into the HIBOU modular architecture.

papers.title: Machine Learning Meets High-Energy Nuclear Physics: From Pattern Recognition to Physics-Integrated Discovery
papers.short_authors: Xun Chen, Weiyao Ke, Yu-Gang Ma, Long-Gang Pang, Kai Zhou
papers.abstract: A mini-review surveys physics-integrated ML in heavy-ion collisions, neutron stars, lattice QFT, and QCD, emphasizing physical constraints, uncertainty quantification, and validation.

papers.title: Physics-informed interpretable forms for dipole resonances and quantities relevant for astrophysics
papers.short_authors: Gourab Banerjee, Jhilam Sadhukhan, Debasish Mondal, B. K. Agrawal, Chandrani Sen, S. Mukhopadhyay
papers.abstract: Bayesian inference extracts IVGDR parameters with explicit nuclear-structure dependence, constraining symmetry-energy coefficients and studying dipole polarizability and neutron-skin correlations.

cautions.title: A Density Functional for Quark Matter with Screened Confinement Interactions
cautions.abstract: The paper derives a quark-matter density functional from a screened linear confinement interaction, with an interaction energy density proportional to n^(2/3).
